title: Today Is the Deadline: Webb County Must Certify Its Nov. 3 Election Results
excerpt: Today, Tuesday, November 17, is the last day Webb County has to formally certify the results of the November 3 general election. Several local races still have no certified winner.
content:
Today, Tuesday, November 17, is the last day Webb County has to formally certify the results of the November 3 general election. Under Texas law, the local canvass must happen no earlier than the third day after the election and no later than the 14th day — and today is day 14, according to an advisory from the Texas Secretary of State’s office.

The canvass is the step where county election officials formally review and certify the precinct-level results before they feed into the statewide tally. Until it happens, the results remain unofficial.

As of this morning, Webb County had not posted a certification. Webb Watch 956 checked the county’s official results page and found it still blank; the unofficial results page still carried only the documents posted on November 3. No canvass or certification statement for Webb County or the City of Laredo had appeared in public reporting as of this morning either.

That means several local races still have no certified winner: county treasurer, Laredo City Council Districts 1, 3 and 6, and Municipal Court Judge Place 1. The Associated Press has not called those races.

Unofficially, 60,127 ballots were cast in Webb County — 45,460 during early voting, about 76 percent of the total, and 13,740 on Election Day, according to the county’s unofficial count reported by KGNS.

The mayor’s race is already set for the runoff: no candidate topped 50 percent in the five-candidate field, so District VIII Councilmember Alyssa Cigarroa and incumbent Mayor Victor Trevino advance to a December 12 runoff. Unofficially, Cigarroa led with 19,510 votes (35.5 percent) to Trevino’s 17,725 (32.3 percent), a gap of 1,785 votes out of 54,897 cast in the race.

Cities, school districts and other local entities worked on a slightly earlier clock: their canvasses were due by the 13th day after the election, Monday, November 16.

What the deadline starts

Once the county canvasses, the clock starts on recounts. Candidates and parties have until 5 p.m. on the third business day after the canvass — Friday, November 20, for a canvass completed today — to file a recount petition for county and precinct races. Races with three or more candidates face a tighter deadline: 2 p.m. on the second day after the canvass, Thursday, November 19. The authority must review a recount petition within 48 hours of receiving it.

Webb Watch 956 will publish the certified results for the remaining races as soon as the county posts them.

Update — November 18, 2026

Webb County canvassed the November 3 election results five days before the deadline, at a special Commissioners Court meeting on Thursday, November 12. Elections Administrator Jose Luis Castillo presented the returns, and the court voted 2-0 to canvass the results, with Commissioner Rosaura "Wawi" Tijerina making the motion and Commissioner Ricardo Jaime seconding it, according to the meeting minutes. County Judge Tano Tijerina and Commissioners Jesse Gonzalez and John Galo were absent and excused. No court meeting was held on November 17, the deadline day.

The county has still not posted the certified results online: its "Official Results 2026" page was empty as of early Wednesday, November 18, and the signed canvass document attached to the November 12 minutes could not be opened. The figures below are the county's unofficial final results — the totals presented to the court for the canvass — for the races that had no certified winner:

County treasurer: Esteban Rangel (Democrat) 38,422 votes (68.94%) to Liza Janette Pena (Republican) 17,312 (31.06%). Laredo City Council District 1: Gilbert Gonzalez 4,149 (75.86%) to Lupe De Leon Jr. 1,320 (24.14%). District 3: Melissa R. Cigarroa 3,147 (53.55%), Clarissa "Claire" Cardenas 1,584 (26.95%), Michelle "Mimi" Winterroth 1,146 (19.50%). District 6: D. Tyler King 8,460 (78.38%) to Ubaldo "Baldo" Granados Jr. 2,333 (21.62%). Municipal Court Judge Place 1: Rudy Morales III 27,031 (54.19%) to Nathan Henry Chu 22,848 (45.81%). A total of 60,127 ballots were cast, including 45,460 during early voting and 13,740 on Election Day, according to the county's unofficial final results.

The county has scheduled a risk-limiting audit of the November 3 election for Thursday, November 19, at 9 a.m. at 720 Convent Avenue in Laredo, according to a notice signed November 13. The recount-petition window tied to the November 12 canvass closed November 17, and no recount petition was found for any of the five races above.

Update sources: Webb County Commissioners Court, Nov. 12, 2026 special meeting minutes (county Agendas & Minutes portal); Webb County unofficial final results (DocumentCenter); Webb County Notice of Risk-Limiting Audit, Nov. 13, 2026 (DocumentCenter).

Source: Election Newsdesk, Nov. 17, 2026; Laredo Morning Times via Local National, Nov. 4, 2026.
